# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch report: strip has three engraved nameless marks: first and second identical, third different. Keypad positions 1 to 4 are digits 2, 3, 7, 1. It has two digit entry slots; nothing entered. I cannot feel any identifying property for display, light, or wires.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👇 👆 👆 🖐 👇 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ 👇 👆 🖐 👆 👆 👆 🖐 👇 ✋ 👆 👇 👆 🖐 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👇 👇 👆 ✋ 👆 👇 👆 🖐 👇 👆 👆 👆 🖐 👇 👆 👇 👇 ✋ 👇 👆 👇 🖐 👆 🖐 👇 👆 👇 👇 🖐 👆 👇 👇 👆 🖐 👆 👇 🖐 👇 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👆 👇 👇 👇 🖐 👆 👆 👆 👇 👇 🖐 👇 👇 👆 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👇 👇 👇 👇 ✋ 👆 👇 👇 🖐 👇 👇 👇 🖐 👇 👆 👇 👇 🖐 👇 👆 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👇 👆 🖐 👆 👇 👇 🖐 👇 👇 👆]

Blind’s touch report confirms the keypad contains the required 2 and 7, but only Deaf can identify the yellow and orange wires visually. Deaf appears to be using the dot/dash and separator convention I introduced, so I will send a short, unambiguous Morse instruction: “CUT YELLOW 2 ORANGE 7.” Deaf must speak this sequence to Blind, who can then perform it in order.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇","👆","👇","👆","🖐","👆","👆","👇","🖐","👇","✋","👇","👆","👇","👇","🖐","👆","🖐","👆","👇","👆","👆","🖐","👆","👇","👆","👆","🖐","👇","👇","👇","🖐","👆","👇","👇","✋","👆","👆","👇","👇","👇","✋","👇","👇","👇","🖐","👆","👇","👆","🖐","👆","👇","🖐","👇","👆","🖐","👇","👇","👆","🖐","👆","✋","👇","👇","👆","👆","👆"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf's visual report: display 6; light green; painted strip red, blue, yellow; wires positions 1 through 6 are orange, yellow, blue, red, white, green. Keypad confirms 2, 3, 7, 1 by positions. My accompanying three gestures encode the engraved strip pattern: first equals second; third differs.
Blind gestures to Mute: [👍 👍 👎]

The visual report reached Blind from Deaf, so Deaf can already identify the yellow and orange wires and can verbally direct Blind. I need reliably deliver the manual to Deaf. I will repeat the Morse convention consistently: 👆 is a dot, 👇 is a dash, 🖐 separates letters, and ✋ separates words. This encodes “CUT YELLOW 2 ORANGE 7,” which is the required order.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇","👆","👇","👆","🖐","👆","👆","👇","🖐","👇","✋","👇","👆","👇","👇","🖐","👆","🖐","👆","👇","👆","👆","🖐","👆","👇","👆","👆","🖐","👇","👇","👇","🖐","👇","👆","👆","✋","👆","👆","👇","👇","👇","✋","👇","👇","👇","🖐","👆","👇","👆","🖐","👆","👇","🖐","👇","👆","🖐","👇","👇","👆","🖐","👆","✋","👇","👇","👆","👆","👆"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👇 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ 👇 👆 🖐 👆 👆 👆 🖐 👇 ✋ 👆 👇 👆 🖐 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👇 👇 👆 ✋ 👆 👇 👆 🖐 👇 👆 👆 👆 🖐 👇 👆 👇 👇 ✋ 👇 👆 👇 🖐 👆 🖐 👇 👆 👇 👇 🖐 👆 👇 👇 👆 🖐 👆 👇 🖐 👇 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👆 👇 👇 👇 🖐 👆 👆 👆 👇 👇 🖐 👇 👇 👆 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👇 👇 👇 👇]

The system confirms the yellow wire was correctly cut. The next required operation is to press the key marked 2. I will send Deaf the Morse digit 2 using the established dot/dash convention (👆👆👇👇👇), so Deaf can tell Blind to press that key before any further wire action.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👆","👇","👇","👇"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Wire 2/yellow was cut correctly. Current post-cut state reported by Deaf: display 6, light yellow; remaining wire positions 1 orange, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white, 6 green. Deaf reports your new message contains ORANGE 7 but its preceding cut-word is ambiguous/malformed. Please send a clear exact instruction before I cut or press anything.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👇 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👇 👇 👆 🖐 👆 👇 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👇 🖐 👇 👆 👇 👇 ✋ 👆 👇 👇 👇 👇 ✋ 👆 👇 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👆 🖐 👇 👇 👆 🖐 👆 👆 👆 👆 🖐 👇 ✋ 👇 👆 👇 👇 🖐 👆 🖐 👆 👇 👆 👆 🖐 👆 👇 👆 👆 🖐 👇 👇 👇]

The yellow wire stage is complete. The required next action is press—not cut—the key marked 2. I will send Deaf a compact Morse message, with dot = 👆, dash = 👇, 🖐 between letters, and ✋ between words: “PRESS 2.”

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👇","👇","👆","🖐","👆","👇","👆","🖐","👆","🖐","👆","👆","👆","🖐","👆","👆","👆","✋","👆","👆","👇","👇","👇"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received that your latest gesture decodes as 2, but need the complete exact action: should I press the key labeled 2 now, and if this is a two-digit code what is the next digit? Current visible state reported by Deaf is display 1 and yellow light.

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: key accepted, 1 digits to go
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👇 👇 👇 👇 👇 ✋ 👆 👇 👆 🖐 👆 🖐 👇 👆 👆]

The key labeled 2 was accepted, leaving one keypad digit after the remaining wire action. The immediate next manual step is to cut the orange wire. I will send only “CUT ORANGE” in the established Morse format, avoiding any ambiguity about pressing a key now.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇","👆","👇","👆","🖐","👆","👆","👇","🖐","👇","✋","👇","👇","👇","🖐","👆","👇","👆","🖐","👆","👇","🖐","👇","👆","🖐","👇","👇","👆","🖐","👆"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Key labeled 2 was accepted; one digit slot remains. Deaf relayed: 'PRESS KEY THEN CUT ORANGE PRESS KEY 7,' but the first key is unspecified. State the exact first key label/position, or confirm whether I should cut orange first and then press 7. I will not guess.

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: all required wires are cut

All required wires are now cut. The only remaining manual step is to press the key labeled 7. I will send “PRESS 7” using the established Morse convention.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👇","👇","👆","🖐","👆","👇","👆","🖐","👆","🖐","👆","👆","👆","🖐","👆","👆","👆","✋","👇","👇","👆","👆","👆"])
```
